children: RBL Bank shares fell 8% after Q2 FY27 profit surged 170%, as brokerages differed on the lender’s earnings recovery, valuations and return outlook

RBL Bank shares fell as much as 8 per cent to Rs 388 on the BSE on 13 October 2026, despite the lender reporting a 170 per cent year-on-year rise in second-quarter net profit to Rs 482 crore. The decline came as brokerages differed on the bank’s earnings recovery, valuation and return prospects following its Q2 FY27 results. The bank’s net interest income (NII) rose 37 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,131 crore, while operating profit increased 92 per cent to Rs 1,396 crore. However, higher provisions and concerns over the pace of improvement in asset quality and profitability continued to shape analyst assessments.

Citi maintained a positive view of RBL Bank’s recovery prospects, with a target price of Rs 505, reflecting expectations of an improvement in return on assets (RoA). Goldman Sachs retained its Sell rating, citing muted retail loan growth and a slower pace of improvement in credit costs.

CLSA also remained cautious, setting a target price of Rs 310 and flagging valuation concerns in relation to the bank’s medium-term return on equity (RoE) prospects. The differing recommendations reflect uncertainty over whether the lender can translate its improved quarterly earnings into sustainable returns. While the sharp rise in profit signals a recovery from the year-ago period, analysts remain focused on the quality and durability of that improvement.

RBL Bank’s gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio improved to 1.02 per cent from 2.32 per cent a year earlier, while its net non-performing asset (NNPA) ratio declined to 0.29 per cent from 0.57 per cent. The bank reported a RoA of 0.92 per cent and a RoE of 4.43 per cent. The lender plans to deploy surplus liquidity into wholesale banking and secured retail lending while strengthening its granular deposit base and managing funding costs.

The pace of loan growth, deposit mobilisation and credit-cost normalisation will remain key factors in determining its profitability trajectory. For investors, the contrasting brokerage views underline the distinction between a strong year-on-year profit increase and a sustained improvement in returns. The bank’s ability to expand lending profitably while protecting margins and improving returns will be central to its valuation outlook.
